candidates.name: eCommerce-dataset-samples
candidates.what_it_holds: Bright Data (formerly Luminati) org repo of committed sample datasets, one per retailer, each >1,000 records, in JSON/NDJSON/CSV/Parquet (optionally gzipped). Sites covered: Amazon, Walmart, Target, eBay, Zara, Home Depot, plus more. Fields (~17 per record): title, ASIN/product id, URL, initial_price, final_price, currency, availability/inventory, reviews_count, rating, description, categories, brand, features, images_count, image_url, seller info, delivery details. Described as subsets of larger paid datasets with 'millions of records'; no dates/geography stated in README, 91 stars, updated 13 Sep 2026 (actively maintained).
candidates.why_useful: Directly the requested template: a real, committed multi-retailer price/rank/review-count dataset schema (price, rating, review velocity, availability) that is the closest open analogue to what a scraped Airbnb search-page panel would need to look like for point-in-time price/availability nowcasting. Useful as a schema/format reference for the team's own fee-panel search-page capture (rule #6) and for gap #2 (realised price/occupancy proxies) methodology, even though it is retail not travel.
candidates.size_hint: >1,000 records per sample file across ~6+ retailers; full paid dataset described as millions of rows
candidates.geography: not stated (likely US-centric given US retailers listed)

candidates.name: Similarweb-free-API
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client hitting an undocumented (but public, key-free) Similarweb browser-extension endpoint. Returns per-domain: total visits, global rank, country rank, bounce rate, geo split, traffic sources, screenshot, category. No data committed; it is a live-pull method, not a dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Directly answers gap #5 (web-traffic estimates / Similarweb-like engagement data) with a genuinely free, no-API-key route to Similarweb-grade domain rank and traffic-source data for airbnb.com (and BKNG/EXPE/VRBO domains) that could be pulled going forward as a point-in-time engagement series if the team decides to run it (a ToS question per rule #6 since it touches a scraping-adjacent endpoint, even though the target is not airbnb.com's booking flow).
candidates.size_hint: N/A - live API client, no stored data
candidates.time_coverage: N/A (point-in-time pulls only, no historical archive)

candidates.name: amazon-scraper-python
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed, non-official Python client for scraping Amazon product listing pages (price, rating, review count, title) from search results. No data committed, pure client code, 878 stars, actively maintained (updated 13 Sep 2026).
candidates.why_useful: A clean, permissively-licensed reference implementation for a search-results scraper (price + rank + rating extraction pattern) that is the closest structural analogue to what an Airbnb search-page fee-panel capture needs to do; useful as a code-pattern template, not as travel data itself.

candidates.name: amazon-reviews-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Apache-2.0 multi-language Amazon review scraper (title, rating, date, body). No dataset committed. 135 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Template for review-velocity-as-demand-proxy methodology (analogous to the team's own Inside-Airbnb reviews-based 'stays index'); could be adapted conceptually, not directly useful as data.

candidates.name: tako-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server (hosted, free tier, no key required to start) exposing 'licensed data the open web does not have': company financials, macro indicators, web and app traffic, sports, US government spending. Wraps TakoData's hosted API at tako.so (external host) rather than committing files.
candidates.why_useful: Potential machine-pullable route to web/app traffic estimates (gap #5) alongside financials, if the free tier actually covers ABNB/BKNG/EXPE domains — worth a human look at the hosted API's coverage and terms before use, since it is a third-party paid-data reseller behind a free tier, not raw open data.
candidates.license: MIT (code wrapper only; underlying data is licensed per repo description)

candidates.name: amazon-scraper (omkarcloud)
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT REST API wrapper for real-time Amazon product/search/review/ranking data across 24 marketplaces. Confirmed via README fetch: no committed dataset files, purely a live-scrape API client.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal — one more scraper template covering multiple country marketplaces (useful only if team ever wants cross-country Amazon price-index comparisons as a consumer-strength proxy); no data value on its own.

candidates.name: Deals-Scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT Canadian multi-site scraper (Facebook Marketplace, Kijiji, eBay, Amazon, Lespac) for deal/price listings. No committed dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Marginal template for cross-platform consumer-pricing scraping; not travel-relevant beyond generic method reference.

candidates.name: price-watch-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server exposing 'verified SaaS price-change history' and a watch-log, backed by ComparEdge's hosted data (external host, not committed to repo).
candidates.why_useful: Not travel/consumer-retail relevant (SaaS pricing only); flagged only as a structural template for point-in-time price-change history capture, which is conceptually close to gap #4 (vintage/point-in-time series) methodology.

candidates.name: commerce-apis
candidates.what_it_holds: Directory/index repo listing '15,000+ E-commerce and real estate APIs' for product data, pricing, reviews, property listings, market research — a link aggregator, not a dataset itself.
candidates.why_useful: Could be useful purely as a discovery index to find a specific retail/real-estate price API later, but it is a link list with no data or working code of its own; low confidence any individual linked API is free or point-in-time.

candidates.name: travel-apis
candidates.what_it_holds: Sibling directory repo from the same author listing '2,000+ Travel APIs for flights, hotels, prices, and destination data' — again a link aggregator with no committed data or code of substance.
candidates.why_useful: Same caveat as commerce-apis: a discovery index only, could point to a niche flight/hotel price API worth a human follow-up, but nothing here is directly usable data.

notes: Direct-hit queries ('web scraped prices dataset', 'amazon best seller rank dataset', 'ecommerce price tracker dataset', 'amazon product ranking scraper', 'bright data dataset samples', 'app store ranking history dataset') all returned EMPTY result sets from gh search repos — the free-text search API appears to require terms that actually appear verbatim in repo metadata; bare/short terms (amazon-scraper, similarweb, --topic=price-tracking) worked far better. 'keepa' collided with unrelated KeePass password-manager repos (no genuine Keepa/Camelcamelcamel price-history mirror surfaced in top results). No real dataset of actual Amazon Best Seller Rank time series (the classic BSR-as-demand-proxy dataset) surfaced anywhere in these searches — worth a WebSearch follow-up by whichever agent owns gap #2/#5 specifically for 'Amazon Best Seller Rank history dataset' and 'Keepa price history export' outside gh search. The strongest find is luminati-io/eCommerce-dataset-samples (real committed multi-retailer schema) and DaWe35/Similarweb-free-API (genuinely free, keyless domain-traffic-and-rank puller applicable to airbnb.com/BKNG/EXPE domains for gap #5 engagement tracking) — flagging the latter as the one candidate worth a second look by the engagement-gap owner. Two gh search repos invocations returned near-total noise (bright data dataset samples: empty; keepa: password managers) confirming this API's free-text matching is brittle; future scouts on retail/ecommerce should lead with bare product/company names (e.g. 'keepa', 'camelcamelcamel', 'rainforest api') rather than descriptive phrases.
